newsitem.title: USA: Gateway 2000 sees rising SGA expenses.
newsitem.headline: Gateway 2000 sees rising SGA expenses.

text.p: Gateway 2000 Inc said on Thursday it expects selling, general and administrative expenses to increase in the fourth quarter of 1996, but to continue to decrease as a percent of sales.
The decrease in percentage reflects seasonal sales growth and increasing leverage of the various systems and infrastructure investments made over the past year, Gateway 2000 said in a statement.

The company reported third quarter earnings of $0.78 a share versus $0.52 last year. SGA expense also rose in the third quarter of 1996 to $143.17 million versus $84.80 million but decreased as a percent of sales to 11.9 percent from 12.3.

"While declining component costs resulted in an average unit price of approximately $2,500, well below the almost $2,700 realized in the second quarter, our direct business model allowed us to improve gross margin and increase profits," said Ted Waitt, chairman and chief executive.

The company's gross margin for the quarter increased to 19.2 percent, up from 18.5 percent in the second quarter of this year. Net shipments for the quarter grew 46.0 percent to a record 474,000 units from 325,000 units during the same period last year, Gateway said.
